title: I made a small prototype game to explore how Antigravity can be used for game development
author: trcxr
selftext:
Hey everyone

I’ve been experimenting with Antigravity as a tool for game development, and I wanted to share a small prototype I built during this exploration.

The game is called OreBreaker Idle - an incremental 
mining game with a brick-breaker style core loop. A fleet of units bounces through asteroid grids, breaks ore blocks, and drops resources that you can harvest and upgrade over time.

The main goal here isn’t a polished release, but to test:
- how far Antigravity can go for prototyping gameplay systems
- how it handles iteration, logic, and content creation
- where it shines and where it struggles in an actual game scenario

Because of that, this build is very much work-in-progress:
- visuals and balance are rough
- debug elements may still be visible
- mechanics may change or get rebuilt

That said, the core gameplay idea is functional, and I’d genuinely love feedback — especially from other devs curious about AI-assisted tools or incremental/idle design.

Play the prototype on itch.io [here](https://trcxr.itch.io/orebreaker-idle)

Happy to answer questions about the process, Antigravity itself, or future plans for the game. Thanks for checking it out.

comments.author: TwistedSpiral
comments.body: I've been trying it with Godot. Got decently far into the systems but I've reached a point that is not being easily resolved - I've run hundreds of prompts trying to get through this UI issue and it just isn't getting it.

replies.author: trcxr
replies.body:
Yeah, after a point it started hallucinating and I had to step into code and fix it for myself. 
But it was a great way to create a prototype to test if the game is fun. 
This will help a lot as a starting point and then I can expand this in a game engine.

replies.author: fatboyor
replies.body:
to the best of my knowedge, gemni3 doesn't use any game engine. how do you plan to convert it to a engine, maybe like godot?  
it would be really nice there is some programming model that's heavily trained on godot, it's so easy to get to a point things get stuck

replies.author: trcxr
replies.body: You are right, gemini3 doesn't use a game engine. I have some experience with making games in unity. My plan is to recreate this in an engine preferably godot and continue my development their so that I have more control over the design. I would still continue doing experiments and prototyping in Antigravity though.

replies.author: flomller
replies.body: I have a running setup with gemini 3 cli and an open source Godot MCP. Works great in my opinion.

comments.author: Practical-Note-
comments.body:
I tried it out of curiosity.

Useful for small things, useless for practically anything real. It becomes unable to follow its own code quickly, duplicates functions, etc.

The fact that it can play Pang or Tetris doesn't impress me.

Even so, its ability to create nodes, locate elements, configure parameters, etc makes it a useful tool.

comments.author: idog63
comments.body:
Just getting started with vibe coding so I was impressed that antigravity created a decent Suika clone in about 4 minutes. It uses matter.js for physics and it is pretty good! I've improved it a bit by working on the code manually and I swapped out the fruit sprites for pics of my grandson :)

I found a zip file online with the real Suika sound effects as .wav files. Asked antigravity to implement the sound effects and it worked great first try.

Deployed it to Azure static web apps and now my family can try it out on their iPad / iPhones.

[https://red-sky-01800311e.2.azurestaticapps.net/](https://red-sky-01800311e.2.azurestaticapps.net/)
